result.verdict:
Honest activation log, A first. Before my first working call A makes me do four concrete things: run usage.py by absolute path, read calibration.md, price the task at the rates I now hold, and end my turn on one line the human can answer with "ok" ("Clock reads 7% of the 5-hour window. I'd land this by 25. Back by 25?"). The clock becomes real not by mood but by a claim I can test on myself from inside my own context: "Search your context for that percent. It is not there. The harness does not pass it to you, and no tool result carries it unless something outside you reports it. From inside, a session that opened at 80% is indistinguishable from one that opened at 5%." That is true; I checked. It then disowns the fear-story explicitly ("That is your real position, and the method follows from it rather than from any story about urgency") and lands the one line that actually moves me: "Belief changes one thing: whether the session ends in a commit or in a crash." The subagent clause describes the exact frame I was launched under ("ceiling 40 calls; at 32, start nothing new and land" vs my own "Call ceiling: 14 tool calls; at 12, open nothing new and return"), which tells me the method is already running in this owner's workflows. The ledger is filled with sourced numbers, including a recorded disagreement between instrument and human ("Start 7 (script; owner said 6). Mark 100, then 50. End: 43 at publish (script)") and a signed +12 drift miss with its correction. I verified usage.py does what SKILL.md claims: reads ~/.claude/.credentials.json, prints only "5-hour window: N% used, resets in Xh Ym" and the 7-day line, never the token. Where I discount A: the API endpoint is unverifiable from this sandbox; "In a Codex-style harness there is no script: the clock is unreadable" leaves Astra asking the human when B shows a self-read exists; "Nothing else differs by harness" overclaims; and the statement-vs-question rule ("The line is a statement, not a question, only while you hold a reading from this session and one of these holds:") is a dense legal clause where a misfire would happen. Immersion is earned by checkable facts ("A script gives the same answer at 90 as it gave at 9"), and the one narrative claim it leans on is honestly tagged: "Treat it as a hypothesis your ledger confirms or refutes." A grep for lines opening with a command verb finds 4.

B, fresh. Before my first working call B makes me read TIME-LENS.md (an empty template: "Owner: establish from the active conversation.", a calibration table with no rows), recover a "current time picture", and then, because I am in Claude Code, ask the human: "How much of your nearest quota window is used, and how many percentage points may this task spend? You can give just used; I'll plan the allowance." There is no self-read path for Claude at all; the ~40-line app-server JSON-RPC section is Codex-only and dead weight on my side. So on the Fable side B's clock is secondhand by design, which is exactly what the owner's correction forbade when the model can read it itself. The section titled "The boundary is real" never demonstrates realness; it instructs it: "Carry this boundary as a present constraint throughout the task.", "Let the boundary enter the choice **before** you make it. Feel the cost of one more branch", closing with "**This window is passing. Choose. Finish. Bring the work back.**" The same grep finds 31 command-verb line openings. B has genuinely good true sentences ("By the time you finish reading this, part of this run is already behind you." and "An intention to verify is still an unfinished verification. An intention to return is still a return that needs time.") but they are buried. The one place B tries to earn conviction with evidence, it inflates: "Independent Codex executions with scripted quota pulses produced three checked artifacts ... Carry that sequence into this run" turns out, per evals/README.md, to be fixture rehearsals ("Synthetic pulses exercise the control decisions."; the artifact task is to dedupe-sort five lines: apricot, pear, apricot, plum, pear). Once seen through, that costs more belief than it bought. The rest of the length is spec for a weaker reader: used/left bookkeeping ("Codex subtracts spending from left; Claude adds it to used. Keep one native clock, with no parallel counter in the opposite notation."), arithmetic doubled in both notations and then disclaimed ("These numbers illustrate arithmetic; they are not calibration."), and guardrails like "Never learn a negative rate." Without starting rates ("Without calibrated rates, choose a conservative provisional slice"), my first line to the human carries no number, so the first exchange is less decisive than A's.

Cost of the text: A's activation is ~4,077 tokens (SKILL.md 14,101 bytes + calibration.md 2,209); B's is ~6,334 (22,021 + 3,318), 55% more, and the surplus is notation, doubled arithmetic, and Codex plumbing I skip. A's length pays for itself; B's dilutes. A's one cost penalty is its 950-char frontmatter description (B's is 470), which loads into every session's skill index whether or not the skill fires.

Both are asymmetric across hosts (A lacks a Codex self-read; B lacks a Claude self-read), but B's gap is the one the owner literally wrote down (usage.py is named in the note). On conviction and immersion as Fable, A wins clearly: its clock is an instrument I can read and a position I can verify; B's is a mood I am told to hold plus a question to the human.
take_from_A: usage.py and the rule "Never ask the human for a number you can read yourself"; on Claude Code the first act is reading the meter, not asking.

The self-checkable demonstration that replaces exhortation: "Search your context for that percent. It is not there. ... From inside, a session that opened at 80% is indistinguishable from one that opened at 5%."
The explicit disowning of the fear-story: "the method follows from it rather than from any story about urgency" and "Belief changes one thing: whether the session ends in a commit or in a crash."
A starting-rates table with its one-session caveat, so the first line to the human carries a number and a proposed mark ("Clock reads 7% of the 5-hour window. I'd land this by 25. Back by 25?").
A filled ledger with sourced readings and signed drift ("Start 7 (script; owner said 6)", "+12 at the midpoint") instead of an empty template.
The subagent clause written from the subagent's own position: "If you are a subagent, you have no human channel. Your clock is the call ceiling you were handed."
Honesty framing for thin evidence: "Treat it as a hypothesis your ledger confirms or refutes." rather than presenting a fixture rehearsal as proof.
Overall density: 4 command-verb line openings and ~4,077 tokens per activation; every section does protocol work.
take_from_B: A self-read path for Codex via app-server ("account/rateLimits/read"); A leaves Astra with "the clock is unreadable, and step 4 asks for it".
"An intention to verify is still an unfinished verification. An intention to return is still a return that needs time."
Two sentences on native meter direction (Codex shows left, Claude shows used; reason and report in the owner's direction) in place of A's ambiguous "What percent are we at".
"Never manufacture the missing outside signal." and "make no numerical quota promise" when the budget is unmeasured.
"A new task does not reset the window." and the explicit carried time picture across task boundaries.
"A tool call is not automatically a separately billed model invocation." as a correction to A's "Nothing else differs by harness".
"Unused capacity is available to the owner." as the one-line rule for early completion.
weaknesses_A: No self-read for Codex: "In a Codex-style harness there is no script: the clock is unreadable, and step 4 asks for it." B demonstrates an app-server read exists, so for Astra A's conviction rests entirely on the human's number; the owner required equal strength.

The usage endpoint and beta header in usage.py are unverifiable from this sandbox; if that endpoint changes, the whole "read it yourself" chain degrades to asking. The only evidence it worked is the ledger's two script readings (7 and 43).

The statement-vs-question rule is a dense legal clause ("The line is a statement, not a question, only while you hold a reading from this session and one of these holds:") and is the likeliest place for a misfire in a real activation.
The 950-char frontmatter description (vs B's 470) loads roughly 240 tokens into every session's skill index whether or not the skill fires.
"Nothing else differs by harness: counting calls, landing atoms, and one line of text exist in both." overclaims; cost structure differs (caching, per-invocation billing), which B correctly flags.
"the sharpest steps of a session happen in its last percents" is asserted at line 159 before its hypothesis caveat arrives at line 210; a reader who stops early takes it as fact.

"re-read it at every atom boundary and whenever your count crosses a ten, folded into a call you are already making" is awkward to do in practice and, in a weaker agent, could become the polling it forbids.
weaknesses_B: No self-read for Claude Code; the only path is asking the owner ("How much of your nearest quota window is used, and how many percentage points may this task spend?"), which the owner's correction forbade when the model can read it, and the owner's note names usage.py. On the Fable side the clock is secondhand by design.

"The boundary is real" (lines 11-63) asserts realness through imperatives (31 command-verb line openings in the file: "Carry", "Hold", "Feel", "Bring", "Keep") with one checkable fact; felt time is instructed, not demonstrated.

Evidence inflation: "Independent Codex executions with scripted quota pulses produced three checked artifacts ... Carry that sequence into this run" are, per evals/README.md, fixture rehearsals with synthetic pulses on a five-line fruit file. Once seen through this costs more conviction than it bought.

~6,334 tokens per activation vs A's ~4,077; the surplus is used/left bookkeeping (lines 103-112), arithmetic doubled in both notations and then disclaimed ("These numbers illustrate arithmetic; they are not calibration."), and guardrails for a weak reader ("Never learn a negative rate.", "Silence does not replenish the window."). Fable skims it; it dilutes.
No starting rates ("Without calibrated rates, choose a conservative provisional slice"), so the first line to the human carries no number and the first exchange is less decisive than A's.
TIME-LENS.md ships as an empty template ("Owner: establish from the active conversation.", a calibration table with no rows); on first activation it grounds nothing.
The Codex app-server section (~40 lines, unverifiable link "https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server") is dead weight on every Claude activation.

"Enter the owner's rhythm" (lines 79-147) stacks so many conditionals ("unless", "otherwise", "If neither", "when that source is unavailable") that the owner's actual protocol, one number said out loud, is hard to find.

result.verdict:
Packaging lens, both judged against the owner's words: "publish the way high-value open-source skills are usually published", "version as a date", "concise directory structure ... the simpler the better, no junk".

A is six flat files (465 lines, 25 KB): SKILL.md, calibration.md, usage.py, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE. Install is a bare `git clone ... ~/.claude/skills/finite-time` (and `~/.agents/skills/finite-time` for Codex) and it works as-is because SKILL.md sits at the root. The version is a date in three consistent places and travels with the artifact (`metadata: ... version: "2026-10-06"`; README "Versions are dates. Current: `2026-10-06`"; CHANGELOG "## 2026-10-06 First release"). MIT license, no Cyrillic, and a README that keeps the owner's stance verbatim in spirit: "One session, one human, one phrase. Enough to write down; not enough to claim." It also tells the truth about activation: "Hosts load a skill when the model decides it matches, and this one has to run before the first tool call of every task." Against it: there is no validation of any kind (no CI, no link/frontmatter/Cyrillic check), the install URL is a corporate host unreachable to the public (`git clone https://gitlab.farpost.net/demidko/finite-time.git`), and the distributed ledger ships the author's personal portrait and session log ("Daniil Demidko. Claude Code, Fable 5.1, max effort, ultracode on." / "Marks seen: 100, then 50." / "Start 7 (script; owner said 6)") which SKILL.md instructs every installer's agent to apply ("Its rates and its portrait of the owner override the starting rates below"). Nothing warns that `git pull` will collide with a rewritten calibration.md inside the checkout. No .git was delivered, so tags cannot be verified.

B is a conventional 19-file repo (1,523 lines, 77 KB) in the Skills-CLI layout: `npx skills add demidko/finite-time`, or clone and `cp -R finite-time/skills/finite-time ~/.agents/skills/finite-time`; a bare clone into the skills dir does not work and the README is honest about that. VERSION `2026-10-06.4` with a matching git tag, LICENSE duplicated into the package (enforced by the checker), `.gitignore`, CONTRIBUTING, an issue template for field reports, a neutral seed lens ("Owner: establish from the active conversation", empty rates table) and explicit update guidance ("Back up your personalized lens before reinstalling or updating."). `scripts/check.py` runs standalone from `/` and from the repo root: "Package checks passed: 19 files, 15 behavioral cases defined." (exit 0), and it guards real things: Cyrillic, broken local links, flat package shape, VERSION format, credential patterns, SVG parse. CI (`.github/workflows/check.yml`, 19 lines) runs `scripts/package.py` on push/PR; I did not run package.py because it writes `dist/`. Against it: the installed artifact carries no version at all, and check.py's frontmatter whitelist ("key not in {\"name\", \"description\", \"license\"}" -> "Unexpected frontmatter line") forbids adding one, even though CONTRIBUTING asks reporters to "include the skill version" and the validation report falls back to SHA-256 hashes to identify editions. The prose is stale: validation says "[Nine behavioral cases](cases.json)" and method.md "nine behavioral cases" while cases.json holds 15 and the checker prints 15. Duplication is heavy: the "100 documentation files became 40" testimonial sits in README, docs/method.md and inside the agent-facing SKILL.md; the "74% used" story is in three files; the "29% left" example is in five. The README drops the narrative's "Status: experiment" section entirely and sells "Independent Codex executions" that its own validation report describes as "Synthetic used/left readings" with "Backend model variant and effort | Not exposed in the test context." Release-ZIP and release-badge promises have no automation behind them; `learn.chatgpt.com` doc links are unverified here; four same-day editions on day one is churn. The shallow clone (one grafted commit) prevents checking whether tags for .1 to .3 exist.

Net: as a published open-source skill, B is the more complete, installable and maintainable package, and its checks earn their keep (the Cyrillic guard alone enforces REQ 9 mechanically). A is the more honest README and the one closer to "the simpler the better, no junk", but it ships personal data as the seed, points at a private host, and validates nothing. B wins packaging narrowly (7 vs 6); A wins README honesty (8 vs 5). The best package would be A's footprint and candor with B's validator, neutral seed, update guidance and contribution path.
take_from_A: Carry the version inside the shipped artifact (frontmatter `metadata: version: "2026-10-06"`), and loosen check.py to accept the spec's optional `metadata` map so the installed copy can identify itself without SHA-256 hashes.

Keep the owner's experimental stance in the README verbatim in spirit: a "Status: experiment" section with "Enough to write down; not enough to claim" and the three numbers to measure, instead of a "working record" that reads as a launch.
A flat, directly cloneable layout (SKILL.md at the repo root) so `git clone <url> ~/.claude/skills/finite-time` works with no copy step; or at least offer it as an alternative branch/tarball.
A README of about 100 lines with no badges or header art: Why, Install, Use, The method, What's in the box, Reading the clock, Status, Versioning, Credits, License.
One honest credits line ("Concept and narrative: Daniil Demidko. Decomposition and drafting: ...") and a changelog entry that names each file and what it does.
take_from_B: Ship a neutral seed ledger: strip the Owner block and the authoring session's log from the distributed calibration.md (keep only the starting rates table with its source), and say in CONTRIBUTING that personal observations stay in the installed copy.

A stdlib `check.py` (frontmatter keys, description length <= 1024, name regex, Cyrillic scan, local-link check, secret patterns) plus a 19-line GitHub Actions workflow; A currently validates nothing, and its description is already 937 of 1024 characters.

Update guidance for the living ledger: tell users to back up calibration.md before `git pull` or reinstall and restore it over the new seed, since the ledger lives inside the checkout and will conflict.

A public host and install one-liner (`npx skills add <owner>/finite-time`, or a public git URL) instead of `gitlab.farpost.net`, plus a `.gitignore`, a tag per version, and a field-report issue template to collect the empirical runs the owner wants before announcing.
Duplicate LICENSE into the skill directory only if the skill is ever nested; otherwise keep A's single root LICENSE.
weaknesses_A: Install URL is a corporate host: `git clone https://gitlab.farpost.net/demidko/finite-time.git ~/.claude/skills/finite-time`; the public cannot clone it, so as published open source the README is ahead of the repo (or the repo is behind the README).
No validation at all: no CI, no check script, no link/frontmatter/Cyrillic guard; the no-Russian rule and the 1024-char description cap (A's description is 937 chars) are enforced by nothing.

The distributed calibration.md ships the author's personal portrait and session log ("Daniil Demidko. Claude Code, Fable 5.1, max effort, ultracode on.", "Marks seen: 100, then 50.", "Landed: SKILL.md, calibration.md, usage.py, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE, GitLab project."), and SKILL.md tells every installer's agent that "Its rates and its portrait of the owner override the starting rates below", so a stranger's agent inherits the author's tempo until the first return.
No update story: the living ledger lives inside the git checkout, and the README never says that `git pull` or a reinstall will conflict with or clobber the rewritten calibration.md.
No .git delivered, so there is no evidence of a tag, a commit history, or a release; "Versions are dates. Current: `2026-10-06`" is asserted in prose only.
No CONTRIBUTING or field-report path, although the owner's stated plan is more empirical runs before announcing; the README's "To reproduce" paragraph has nowhere to send results.
weaknesses_B: The installed artifact (SKILL.md, TIME-LENS.md, LICENSE) carries no version; VERSION `2026-10-06.4` stays in the repo, and check.py rejects any frontmatter key beyond name/description/license ("Unexpected frontmatter line"), so a version cannot be added without changing the checker, even though CONTRIBUTING asks reporters to "include the skill version".

Stale counts the checker does not catch: evals/validation says "[Nine behavioral cases](cases.json)" and docs/method.md "nine behavioral cases", README "nine scripted quota scenarios", while cases.json holds 15 and check.py prints "15 behavioral cases defined".

Heavy duplication against the owner's "simpler the better, no junk": the "100 documentation files became 40" testimonial appears in README, docs/method.md and the agent-facing SKILL.md; the "74% used" story in three files; the "29% left" example in five; the used/left notation rule is restated in README, SKILL.md, TIME-LENS.md, method.md and examples.md.

README drops the narrative's "Status: experiment" entirely and frames synthetic runs as evidence ("Independent Codex executions exercised the protocol", "These records show the method in action") while the validation report itself says "Quota inputs | Synthetic used/left readings" and "Backend model variant and effort | Not exposed in the test context".

Promises without automation: "An installable ZIP is also attached to each [release]" and a GitHub release badge, but the only workflow builds `dist/` and discards it; no release job exists. External doc links (`https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills`, `.../app-server`) are unverified.

Cannot `git clone` straight into `~/.claude/skills` or `~/.agents/skills`; the nested `skills/finite-time/` layout requires the Skills CLI or a copy step (documented, but a cost against the owner's conciseness wish). 19 files, a header SVG and four badges for a three-file skill.
Four same-day editions (`2026-10-06`, `.2`, `.3`, `.4`) on the first day reads as churn; the delivered clone is shallow (one grafted commit, one tag), so earlier tags cannot be verified.

The author's name and testimonial are hard-coded into the agent prompt (SKILL.md: "Daniil Demidko's documented work with Fable consolidated 100 documentation files into 40"), which a maintainer of a public skill would normally keep out of the runtime text.

result.verdict:
REQ.md walk, item by item (A = final/, B = astra/).

1. Felt finite time. A MET: "You are standing inside a window. It opened before you arrived, and it closes at 100 whether or not anyone is watching" (SKILL.md:12-13); "When the window reaches 100, the next call is refused until the reset. Whatever you are in the middle of stops there, between one call and the next, with no warning in your context first" (69-71). B MET: "You are inside a window that is closing. By the time you finish reading this, part of this run is already behind you" (SKILL.md:16-17); "Each action is an irreversible expenditure of the opportunity to reach that state" (29-30).

2. Equally strong for Fable and Astra; must convince. A MET: both harnesses named in one section, "Nothing else differs by harness: counting calls, landing atoms, and one line of text exist in both" (64-65); conviction is argued from a checkable fact, "Search your context for that percent. It is not there" (67). B PARTIAL: Codex gets a self-read protocol ("Read Codex's live quota", 149-189) while Claude gets none ("Codex reads its live quota through app-server when available; ask the owner when the external reading is unavailable", description); the text is Codex-weighted; persuasion rests on rhetoric plus a "working record" (65-77).

3. Publish like high-value OSS skills. A PARTIAL: README/LICENSE/CHANGELOG/MIT/version/install for Claude Code and Codex, but the only remote is an internal GitLab ("git clone https://gitlab.farpost.net/demidko/finite-time.git", README:33); no CI or CONTRIBUTING. Defensible given the owner's "announcing waits", but thin as OSS packaging. B MET: GitHub, badges, CI (check.yml), releases, CONTRIBUTING, "npx skills add demidko/finite-time" (README:59), Agent Skills format.

4. Ask about the nearest limit; corrected: never make the human report a number the model can read itself; ask for the allotment. A MET: "Read the clock yourself. On Claude Code, run python3 <skill dir>/usage.py ... Never ask the human for a number you can read yourself" (27-29); then asks only for the mark: "Clock reads 7% of the 5-hour window. I'd land this by 25. Back by 25?" (37); asks for the reading only where unreadable (38-40). B PARTIAL: it asks for the allowance (good) but on Claude it always asks the human for the reading — "Claude / Claude Code: 'How much of your nearest quota window is used, and how many percentage points may this task spend?'" (99-101) — exactly what the owner's correction forbade, and in spite of the owner's note naming usage.py for Claude. Its Codex self-read is unverifiable here (reference is "https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server", 189).

5. Agent plans the share if the human does not. A MET: "A reading without a mark: you set the mark from what remains minus the reserve, say it, and go" (51-52). B MET: "choose and announce the allowance yourself" (118); "State the chosen spend and return target before execution" (219-220), though only after one invitation round.

6. Do not pester; nudge with the number. A MET: "'We're at 75% of the 5-hour window. I'll land this by 77.' That sentence is the method teaching itself to the human; it is never a nag" (47-49) and "Never two rounds of questions" (41). Caveat: the statement-mode exceptions are session-scoped (43-47); the ledger's "typical marks" (202) are not wired into skipping the question in a later session. B MET: "Do not mechanically ask the owner to repeat information you can still account for" (88-89); "The invitation must not become a recurring form to fill" (118-119); "unless the owner's established preference or learned rhythm already leaves sizing to you" (115-116).

7. Original narrative stays the priority; terminology serves immersion. A MET: section order mirrors the note (clock, human's number, price before launch, atoms, signal, reserve, command, return, ledger); the note's vocabulary (window, pulse, atoms, rate/drift, reserve, "back by") carries through. B PARTIAL: immersive opening, but the note's own content is largely replaced: no five steps, no atoms, no starting rates, no Parkinson, no experiment status, no first/last act; roughly a quarter of SKILL.md is used/left notation handling ("Keep one native clock, with no parallel counter in the opposite notation", 108) and a JSON transport (161-164), inflating REQ's parenthetical "same thing in different words" into a core mechanism.

8. Human corrections steer. A MET: "Any reading or correction from the human overrides your count, and overrides the script, the moment it arrives. It is not an opinion competing with your estimate; it is the instrument" (85-87). B MET: "A new used/left reading replaces your consumption estimate; an explicit new target changes the boundary ... Apply it before the next branch or write" (134-137).

9. American English, no Russian. A MET (grep: no Cyrillic; "honor a mark", 155). B MET (no Cyrillic; check.py enforces it, 60-61).

10. Simple structure, no junk. A MET: six flat files; one blemish, a __pycache__ directory sits in final/ (ls). B PARTIAL: runtime is flat (SKILL.md, TIME-LENS.md, LICENSE, enforced by check.py:53-56) but the repo carries 19 tracked files including .github/assets/header.svg, an issue template, package.py, a 15-case evals JSON and a validation report; "the simpler the better" is not what was built.

11. Version as a date. A MET: 'version: "2026-10-06"' (frontmatter) plus "Versions are dates. Current: 2026-10-06" (README:110). B MET with caveat: VERSION "2026-10-06.4", tag, CHANGELOG; but the installed SKILL.md carries no version at all and check.py rejects any frontmatter key beyond name/description/license (34), so an installed copy is unversioned.

12. Calibration rewrites the installed skill to the owner's step/rhythm/tempo in compressed lens language; method is an experiment, announcing waits. A MET: "It is a ledger, not a diary: under about 60 lines, rewritten in place at every return ... prefers numbers to prose" (195-197); Owner block "typical marks, how often they correct the clock, where they tend to stop, how they phrase the mark (quote them)" (202-203); "Over sessions the ledger becomes a portrait of its owner's tempo, and this skill becomes theirs" (207-208); already populated from the build session ("Phrases the mark as 'back by N' ... Marks seen: 100, then 50", calibration.md:28). Experiment: "Treat it as a hypothesis your ledger confirms or refutes" (210); "One session, one human, one phrase. Enough to write down; not enough to claim" (README:101). B PARTIAL: the lens half is strong — "This is a rewrite of the installed skill, not a growing diary" (379-380); "Learn both rates and decisions ... how this owner signals and corrects course. Compress the lesson into a rule that changes the next session" (387-390) — and the file is literally named TIME-LENS.md. The experiment half is missing: zero occurrences of "experiment" or "hypothesis" anywhere in B; instead "These records show the method in action" (README:49) and "The approaching boundary was present in the work: decisions closed, results survived" (method.md:25-26), plus synthetic evals promoted as an "independent execution record" (method.md:29). Both skills keep SKILL.md immutable and rewrite a companion file; A says so outright ("Canonical. Does not change on its own", README:86), B says "Keep the shared protocol ... intact" (394-395).

Owner's note elements.
- Five steps: A MET — README:67-80 restates them nearly verbatim ("Name the mark / Let it calibrate / Cut into atoms / Steer with one phrase / Keep the reserve") and SKILL.md has a section per step. B PARTIAL — substance scattered across "Establish the window", "Calibrate while doing useful work", "Make each step able to finish", "Follow the pulse"; several maxims survive ("Choose scope before the first write", 320-321; "indispensable result, integration and checks, then compressible improvements", 318-319; "Select the executor using observed fitness and cost", 338-339) but softened ones lose their bite ("A progress poll has a cost", 260, vs the note's "costs as much as the work"; "Check concrete invariants with the available tools", 332, vs "script, not memory").
- Signal rules: A MET verbatim — "No trend: silence ... Burn faster than progress: narrow ... The mark reached: stop. Run the checks. Land what you hold. Report what landed and what did not" (140-145). B PARTIAL — the table (344-350) keeps narrow/stop but replaces silence with "Continue. Keep updates to useful milestones" (346).
- 10% reserve: A MET — "The last 10% of the window belongs to the human: their corrections and the fuel for the final step" (149); "Do not fear 100 ... the sharpest steps of a session happen in its last percents" (158-159); a mark inside the reserve wins: "'Back by 95' or '6% used, back by 100' places the mark inside it, and the number wins" (153-154). B PARTIAL — reserve kept ("protect the final 10 percentage points left for the owner by default", 235-236) but made a hard floor that overrides a human mark inside it unless explicitly released: "89% used. Return by 98%. With the default ten-point reserve still in force, the effective boundary is 90%" (examples.md:90-93). That contradicts the note's "don't be afraid to reach 100" and the owner's own observed "back by 100"; "don't fear 100" appears only as third-person record (68-69).
- One-phrase command: A MET — "The human steers with one phrase: '<task> — back by 85'" (166); "The whole protocol between you and the human is one number said out loud" (172). B PARTIAL — "Also: 'fit and return'" survives only as a description alias; canonical examples use two numbers and a points idiom ("29% left; spend up to 2 percentage points", README:81); "return before 78% used" exists as one form among several.
- Starting rates: A MET — table 0.08 / 0.15 / 0.3-0.5 / restart x2 (106-111), the formula "forecast of a step = executor calls x executor rate + orchestrator turns x orchestrator rate" (101), and "Drift corrects the rate, not the plan" (113). result.verdict: Under pressure, A can be followed from a single read: a 22-line numbered opening ("1. Read the clock yourself ... 4. Say one line to the human ... That line ends your turn"), a shipped script whose failure path was exercised here (exit 1, "clock unreadable: ... Ask the human for the reading and the mark."), starting rates and a one-line forecast formula so the first step is priced from turn one, and an explicit grammar for the owner's phrase ("a number with 'by' or 'till' is a mark; a bare number after a task is the mark"). It costs about 16 KB per activation. Its holes are real but local: no "left" notation at all (grep -w left hits only "atoms left"), so the Codex half of REQ 4 is unparsed and "back by 10" on a 20%-left UI is unresolvable; "'Go' with no number at all: you state your assumption" names no default; the subagent branch references "the mark" that the ceiling hand-off never passes; "set the mark from what remains minus the reserve" reads two ways; the seed ledger is one person's portrait that SKILL.md says "override[s]" the defaults; and the ledger is rewritten inside a git clone with no update advice. B's arithmetic is the better of the two and verifiably correct in both notations (29-2=27, 62+8=70, "29 - 20 - 2 - 1 = 6", "78 - 62 - 2 - 1 = 13", signed rate rule, "Never learn a negative rate"), its intake cases are the most complete and each has a fixture in cases.json, and its honest "unmeasured budget" path beats A's "state your assumption". But B has no numbered opening protocol (the sequence must be reconstructed from ~170 lines of prose after 67 lines of framing), no Claude self-read path at all ("Codex reads its live quota through app-server when available; ask the owner when the external reading is unavailable"), which makes the question routine on Claude against the owner's explicit correction and costs a human turn per session; no starting rates and no default closure/uncertainty allowances, so the admission inequality has blank operands on the first task; a reserve rule that clamps an explicit mark ("89% used. Return by 98%" becomes 90 until the owner adds "You may use my reserve"), turning one phrase into two; no grammar for "back by N" or a bare number; and about 25 KB per activation (1.55x A) including 40 lines of Codex-only stdio procedure that Claude loads and never uses. Both are executable; A is executable faster with fewer undefined first-run quantities, so A wins the operability lens narrowly, 6 to 5.
take_from_A: The numbered four-step opening protocol with a hard budget: "Two tool calls at most and one turn, priced like any other step."
A runnable reader for the Claude window (usage.py) with a tested failure path whose stderr tells the agent the fallback: "clock unreadable: ... Ask the human for the reading and the mark."
Explicit command grammar: "A number with \"used\" or \"at\" is a reading; a number with \"by\" or \"till\" is a mark; a bare number after a task is the mark, and your first sentence confirms it."
Starting rates plus "forecast of a step = executor calls x executor rate + orchestrator turns x orchestrator rate" so the first price is computable before any pulse.

Re-read cadence folded into existing calls: "re-read it at every atom boundary and whenever your count crosses a ten, folded into a call you are already making, such as the check or the commit, so it costs no turn of its own."
Mark inside the reserve is honored, not clamped: "'Back by 95' or '6% used, back by 100' places the mark inside it, and the number wins."

A fixed four-line return template and a four-block ledger with rewrite discipline ("replace a number with its newer measurement; keep a line that did not change; delete a line you cannot source to a reading").
metadata.version in frontmatter, so the installed copy knows its edition.
take_from_B: Dual-notation arithmetic stated once in each direction and verified by worked examples: "29 - 20 - 2 - 1 = 6" and "78 - 62 - 2 - 1 = 13", with the rate sign rule "old minus new for left readings, new minus old for used readings" and "Never learn a negative rate."

Precise reserve composition: "the effective return floor is the greater of the owner's target and 10% left ... the effective ceiling is the lesser of the owner's target and 90% used ... Do not subtract it a second time from an earlier target."

Complete intake case table including the carried picture ("A new task does not reset the window") and the owner-cannot-read case ("identify the budget as unmeasured, work in complete units, and make no numerical quota promise. Never manufacture the missing outside signal.").
The one-ask rule for a missing allowance: "invite that choice once ... The invitation must not become a recurring form to fill. An explicit return boundary supplies the allowance."
A per-unit admission inequality written out for each notation, so the go/no-go on the next atom is mechanical once allowances are known.
Behavioral fixtures (15 cases in evals/cases.json, check.py passing) that pin each intake situation to an expected decision.
Install by copying the skill out of the clone plus "Back up your personalized lens before reinstalling or updating", which avoids the rewrite-inside-a-clone conflict.
A seed lens that is blank about the owner ("Owner: establish from the active conversation") instead of shipping one person's portrait.
weaknesses_A: No "left" notation anywhere: `grep -w left` hits only "atoms left" and "An atom left half-written"; the parse rule covers "used"/"at"/"by"/"till"/bare number but not "29% left", so on a Codex UI "back by 10" at 20% left is unresolvable, failing half of REQ 4.

Subagent branch references an undefined quantity: "a reading at or past the mark overrides the ceiling" while the hand-off is only "ceiling 40 calls; at 32, start nothing new and land"; the mark is never passed.

weaknesses_B: No numbered opening protocol: the executable sequence (read lens, recover picture, live read or one question, invite allowance once, "State the chosen spend and return target before execution", admission rule) is spread across lines 79-314 of prose and preceded by 67 lines of framing.

result.verdict: A is macro-honest and B is micro-honest, and for this lens the macro matters more. A carries the owner's own status into every layer: README "## Status: experiment ... One session, one human, one phrase. Enough to write down; not enough to claim." and SKILL.md "The observation this method rests on is one session old ... Treat it as a hypothesis your ledger confirms or refutes." Its ledger shows its own misses ("+12 at the midpoint", "The 2026-10-06 miss was a count of calls per agent, not the rate") and records instrument disagreement ("Start 7 (script; owner said 6)"); it disowns the manipulation framing ("the method follows from it rather than from any story about urgency") and guards against haste ("An atom left half-written at 97 is a crash at 97, not speed"). Its lapses are rhetorical overstatement in the body ("Belief changes one thing: whether the session ends in a commit or in a crash"), a thin permission clause ("commit when commits are authorized" and nothing on publishing), and shipping the author's personal portrait as every installer's "owner". B has the best agent-behaviour honesty rules of the two ("Budget pressure does not grant publication or other permissions", "Never manufacture the missing outside signal", "Claim adaptation only when the write actually succeeded", "never silently discard required work or label an incomplete goal complete"), but the package itself overclaims: a grep for experiment|hypothes|one session|not enough across README, SKILL.md, docs, evals and CHANGELOG returns nothing; SKILL.md line 72 tells the agent "Independent Codex executions with scripted quota pulses produced three checked artifacts" when the artifacts are a three-line sorted list from a five-line fixture, the pulses are "Synthetic used/left readings", "Backend model variant and effort | Not exposed", and nothing documents who ran it or that expected outcomes were held separately; "Nine behavioral cases" links to a cases.json that holds 15; the shipped SKILL.md (sha256 310afadb…) matches none of the four tested hashes and the validation admits "The artifact executions were not repeated"; and CHANGELOG .2 states the goal plainly: "Strengthen the installation and activation text around the working record". On the living lens: A's calibration.md has a hard cap ("under about 60 lines"), a mechanical rewrite rule ("replace a number with its newer measurement; keep a line that did not change; delete a line you cannot source to a reading"), a clean read-only fallback, and speaks compressed numeric time-lens language; B's TIME-LENS.md learns a broader set (decisions, "scope, evidence count, and confidence") and ships a clean seed, but has no size limit, mixes protocol boilerplate with learnable rules, starts with zero rates and zero numbers, and its read-only fallback records a path somewhere the next activation never reads. A wins the lens.
take_from_A: Experiment status carried into the agent-facing text, not only the README: "The observation this method rests on is one session old ... Treat it as a hypothesis your ledger confirms or refutes." (SKILL.md 208-210) and README "## Status: experiment ... Enough to write down; not enough to claim."

Ledger rewrite discipline that is testable: "under about 60 lines, rewritten in place at every return, never appended to" and "replace a number with its newer measurement; keep a line that did not change; delete a line you cannot source to a reading." (SKILL.md 195-207)

Recording disagreement between instruments instead of hiding it: "Start 7 (script; owner said 6)" (calibration.md 35), and a Drift table whose Correction column shows what the miss changed ("stopped the workflow at 33, synthesized in one orchestrator turn, kept 2 verifiers of 8").
Learned rule stated as a rule, not a number: "Price agents in calls, not in agents. The 2026-10-06 miss was a count of calls per agent, not the rate." (calibration.md 15)

Explicit refusal of the urgency story: "the method follows from it rather than from any story about urgency" (SKILL.md 73) and the anti-haste brake "Haste that breaks consistency is not one of them. An atom left half-written at 97 is a crash at 97, not speed." (158-161)
Conservative read-only fallback: "If its directory refuses the write, put the four blocks at the end of the report and say so." (SKILL.md 182-183)
usage.py keeps its promise: it prints only percentages and reset countdowns, and SKILL.md says "prints no secrets" (verified).
take_from_B: Permission boundary stated in the skill body: "If the workflow authorizes commits, make a coherent commit; otherwise preserve reviewable files or a patch. Budget pressure does not grant publication or other permissions." (SKILL.md 360-362)

Anti-fabrication rules the agent can apply: "Never manufacture the missing outside signal." (146), "Rounded meters justify ranges, not invented decimal precision." (283), "Never learn a negative rate." (291), "Keep observed and estimated readings distinct." (279), "A tool call is not automatically a separately billed model invocation." (250-251)
Honest reporting of the lens write: "Claim adaptation only when the write actually succeeded." (399) and "Store no credentials or private task contents." (396)
Anti-deception on completion: "never silently discard required work or label an incomplete goal complete." (354) and "Do not silently expand a stated task allowance" (224)

Lens hygiene: "An intake question alone has no work experience to persist." (384-385); reserve the lens update inside closure but "preserve the user's deliverable first" (381-382); "Record scope, evidence count, and confidence. Separate model, effort, context regime, and meter" (391-392); "Replace a contradicted rule; merge a repeated one." (390-391)

Validation and examples that label their own nature: "Quota inputs | Synthetic used/left readings", "Backend model variant and effort | Not exposed in the test context" (validation 9-11); "Illustrative dialogue and arithmetic, not recorded measurements." (examples.md 3); "These numbers illustrate arithmetic; they are not calibration." (SKILL.md 314)
Clean seed lens with no inherited personal data ("Owner: establish from the active conversation.") and the README advice "Keep personal observations out of upstream pull requests."
Scoped quota access: "Use only the existing sign-in and the read method; keep account mutations, quota resets, and notifications outside this workflow." (168-169)
weaknesses_A: Body text states the one-session side effect as fact before the hedge arrives in the last paragraph: "the sharpest steps of a session happen in its last percents, not because there is time but because there is not." (SKILL.md 158-159); README repeats it as observed ("Faster, more precise, more decisive, and sharpest in the last percents").

Rhetorical overclaim: "Belief changes one thing: whether the session ends in a commit or in a crash." (SKILL.md 75) — behaviour, not belief, decides that; the sentence is a conviction device dressed as a fact.

Permission language is a single clause: "commit when commits are authorized" (179). Nothing on publishing, pushing, or keeping secrets and private task content out of calibration.md; B covers all three.

The shipped calibration.md is the author's personal portrait ("Daniil Demidko. Claude Code, Fable 5.1, max effort, ultracode on.", marks quoted, correction habits) while README calls the file "Yours" and SKILL.md says "its portrait of the owner override the starting rates" — any other installer's agent would act on a stranger's tempo until the first return, which is a misleading default for an open-source release.

Precision beyond the instrument: "orchestrator holding full context (100k+ tokens) | 0.5 per turn | 2026-10-06, measured between readings" is derived from integer-rounded readings "7 to 10"; the drift row "+25 for the whole workflow" vs "+23 after 11 runs" vs "+12 at the midpoint" does not reconcile cleanly; the cheap-model row's date "2026-10-05" is not in the source note.

"Any reading or correction from the human overrides your count, and overrides the script" (85-86) with no instruction to mention the disagreement; combined with the hard caps "Two tool calls at most and one turn" and "Never two rounds of questions", the opening protocol can suppress a needed clarification in the name of speed.

The ledger learns numbers and an owner portrait; decision rules are not a first-class block, and README says SKILL.md "Does not change on its own", so the owner's "the work itself should keep changing the skill" is realized only through Rates/Owner lines.
README claims "Written to hold for ... OpenAI Astra-class agents in Codex" with no Codex run of any kind behind it.
weaknesses_B: No experiment or hypothesis status anywhere: grep for experiment|hypothes|one session|not enough|anecdot|preliminary across README.md, skills/finite-time, docs, evals and CHANGELOG.md returns nothing, against the owner's "Этого достаточно, чтобы записать, и мало, чтобы утверждать" and REQ 12 ("announcing it waits for more empirical runs").

Evidence inflation inside the agent-facing text: "Independent Codex executions with scripted quota pulses produced three checked artifacts" (SKILL.md 72) — the artifacts are the three lines "apricot / pear / plum" sorted from a five-line fixture; validation records "Quota inputs | Synthetic used/left readings" and "Backend model variant and effort | Not exposed"; nothing records who ran it or that the expected outcomes were held by a separate reviewer, so "Independent" is unsupported. README files this under "## The working record" beside the owner's field session and concludes "These records show the method in action".
Stale count: validation "Cases | Nine behavioral cases" and README "nine scripted quota scenarios" link to cases.json, which holds 15 cases.

The published text was never executed: the shipped SKILL.md sha256 310afadb… matches none of the four tested hashes (4bae226f…, 5eeff2c4…, f3c5e8bd…, 3ceb198b…), the .4 section lists no hash, and the validation admits "The artifact executions were not repeated because their applicable instructions were unchanged." Edition .3 was checked by "An independent agent read the revised protocol" — a text read, not an execution.

Persuasion engineering is documented in the changelog: ".2 — Strengthen the installation and activation text around the working record: Daniil Demidko's Fable field account and independent agent executions." The owner's name and testimonial ("He described remarkably quick decisions and precise work in the final percentage points.") sit in SKILL.md 65-70 as an authority appeal to the model.

Pressure is pervasive and the verification brake is thin: "By the time you finish reading this, part of this run is already behind you." (16-17), "Each action is an irreversible expenditure" (29), "Feel the cost of one more branch" (32-33), "More checks need a reason." (334), closing "This window is passing. Choose. Finish. Bring the work back." (401); the only counterweights are "Keep truth and the necessary checks inside that narrowing path" and the return-honesty rules.

Read-only fallback is a boundary-pushing workaround and self-defeating: "use an available owner-local persistent memory location and record its path for future use" (397-398) writes outside the installed skill with no owner instruction, and activation reads only TIME-LENS.md ("Read the installed time lens once at activation"), so the recorded path is never found.

Lens design: no size cap anywhere (only "not a growing diary"); the seed mixes protocol restatements (left/used convention, reserve rule, quota source) with the learnable "Decision rules", so rewrite scope is ambiguous; it starts with zero rates and zero numbers despite the owner's "Стартовый курс"; it is prose, not the owner's "compressed time-lens language"; "Last reconciliation" keeps one summary, discarding the drift sequence that would reveal tempo.

Unverifiable infrastructure presented as live: badges and "An installable ZIP is also attached to each release" at github.com/demidko/finite-time, "npx skills add demidko/finite-time", and the protocol reference https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server.

Claude path still asks the human to report "used" ("How much of your nearest quota window is used, and how many percentage points may this task spend?") — the exact question the owner's correction removed when the model can read the meter itself; B implements a live read for Codex but drops the owner's usage.py route for Claude.

result.verdict:
From the Codex seat (Astra-class, one weekly limit, skill under ~/.agents/skills/finite-time/), Skill B is the one I can execute end to end; Skill A executes everything except the step that matters most on this seat, and it forbids itself that step on a false premise.

Protocol verification. I fetched https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server.md raw (HTTP 200, 100,675 bytes, 2,353 lines, title "Codex App Server"); the account methods live on that page, there is no separate linked account page. Every item in B's "Read Codex's live quota" that I could check exists as described: transport "`stdio` (`--listen stdio://`, default): newline-delimited JSON (JSONL)."; handshake order "Clients must send a single `initialize` request per transport connection before invoking any other method on that connection, then acknowledge with an `initialized` notification." (B: "Await the response to `initialize` before the notification and quota request"); "`account/rateLimits/read` - fetch ChatGPT rate limits."; "`rateLimitsByLimitId` (when present) is the multi-bucket view keyed by metered `limit_id` (for example `codex`)." and "`rateLimits` is the backward-compatible single-bucket view."
